EITS-AZURE-001.title: Diagnostic setting deletion followed by role assignment
EITS-AZURE-001.description: Successful diagnostic-setting deletion followed by successful role-assignment creation in the same known subscription and resource tenant, by the same exact actor object and actor-tenant claims within 30 minutes.
EITS-AZURE-001.exact_logic: sql/EITS-AZURE-001.sql; successful diagnosticSettings/delete then roleAssignments/write; exact nonnull subscription/resource tenant/actor object/actor tenant equality; 0 < elapsed <= 1800 seconds
EITS-AZURE-001.why_it_matters: A telemetry export configuration is removed shortly before an access-control assignment is created.
expected_false_positives: Authorized monitoring migration followed by provisioning
Replacement diagnostic setting created before an approved role assignment
EITS-AZURE-001.tuning: Inspect export configuration and change authorization, role definition and assignment recipient. Scope any future exception to subscription, resource tenant, actor object and actor tenant, target resources and expiry; measure missed attacks.
limitations: Requires exact actor object and actor-tenant claims; caller email and IP are not identity keys
Requires known resource tenant context, which is not inferred from token tenant
No correlation across actors or clouds
Equal or missing timestamps cannot establish sequence
A replacement export is contextual counterevidence and does not suppress the baseline
cannot_establish: Malicious intent or absence of authorization
All logging or export delivery stopped
The deleted setting covered the later action
The assigned role is privileged or grants effective access
The role assignment recipient or follow-on use when request details are absent
EITS-AZURE-001.observed: Two Activity Log records report Succeeded: deletion of a diagnostic setting and subsequent creation of a role assignment, with equal known subscription/resource tenant and exact actor object/actor-tenant claims within 30 minutes.
EITS-AZURE-001.inferred: The sequence warrants investigation for possible visibility reduction around access-control changes; intent and impact are unresolved.
